answers.explanation: It's a bridge: radio on one side, Ethernet on the other.
Power over Ethernet: one cable carries both data and power, handy for ceiling-mounted WAPs.
WEP was broken long ago. WPA3 is the current standard.
The name still shows up in connection requests and is easy to sniff. It's a minor deterrent at best.
Separating guests limits what a visitor's device, or a compromised one, can reach.
An admin interface reachable from the internet is a target.
Frames between VMs on the same host travel through it and never touch a physical wire.
Traffic shaping keeps one VM from starving the rest.
A balloon driver in the guest inflates to hand unused memory back to the hypervisor.
Role Based Access Control, also called authorizations.
